profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point in Siena, Italy, tagged telecom=data_center, is named E. D. Accounting Siena. The word "Accounting" in the business name plainly identifies this as an accounting or bookkeeping practice serving local clients, not a data center or IT hosting business. Accounting firms maintain their own office computing and, in many cases, client financial-record servers, but that is a fundamentally different function from a commercial colocation or cloud data center. The telecom=data_center tag on this point is best explained as a mapping error applied to the firm's own small server room or network closet, and this entry records that determination plainly rather than inventing data-center specifications for an accounting office.

reading.body:
OpenStreetMap tagging errors can place non-data-center facilities into infrastructure databases, potentially distorting regional AI capacity maps.

This entry in Siena, Italy was tagged as a data center but is actually an accounting firm's office. The name itself identifies the business function plainly. Accounting practices maintain their own server rooms for client records and internal IT, but this is office infrastructure, not commercial colocation or cloud hosting. The mismatch likely originated when someone tagged a small server closet with a telecom=data_center label, a common error in crowd-sourced mapping.

For AI infrastructure tracking, this matters because the signal degrades when small office IT gets counted alongside facilities built for compute workloads. A regional inventory that includes an accounting firm's closet server cannot reliably answer questions about actual data center capacity, power draw, or buildable space for AI scaling. The data presented here shows research status as exhausted, meaning further verification is not planned.

This single misclassified point is unlikely to move aggregate numbers meaningfully. But the pattern it illustrates, if widespread, would systematically overstate data center prevalence in regions where office IT infrastructure is common, and undermine confidence in any facility list drawn from unvetted OpenStreetMap tags alone.
